title: Death Toll Surpasses 4,800 Three Weeks After Twin Earthquakes
detail: Three weeks after the June 24 twin earthquakes, Venezuela's government-reported death toll continued climbing, reaching 4,829 as of July 15 — up from 4,734 the day before, 4,333 on July 11, and 2,954 on July 4 — according to figures released by National Assembly President Jorge Rodríguez. More than 16,740 remain injured and tens of thousands are displaced or unaccounted for; an opposition-run missing-persons database organized by María Corina Machado's coalition had logged roughly 36,000 names by early July, far exceeding the government's confirmed dead. USGS's PAGER system had modeled a worst-case toll potentially exceeding 10,000. UN OCHA and the International Rescue Committee continue to warn of secondary health risks — waterborne disease and infection — among displaced families sheltering across La Guaira and Caracas, where the water system has failed in some areas.

media.caption: Venezuela's earthquake death toll rises to 4,829 three weeks after the June 24 quakes
